Lets the app notice that a call is coming in.
Lets the app see the caller\'s number. On Android 9 and later the number is withheld from apps without this permission, so it is the only way to tell a priority caller from anyone else.
Lets the app read a number from the contact you pick. You can also type numbers in by hand instead.
Lets the app ask Do Not Disturb to allow a call through for the length of that call, and put the setting back afterwards.
Lets the app show the alert for a repeat caller.
Lets the repeat-caller alert take over the screen instead of appearing as a banner.
Whether this device lets an app change the ring volume at all.

Backup alert may not be heard

Android tells the app about a call as it starts ringing, not before. The volume is raised during the first moment of the ringtone rather than ahead of it, so the very beginning of the ring may still be quiet.

Everything the app needs has been granted. When an enabled priority contact calls, the app will raise the ring volume, switch out of Vibrate, and ask Do Not Disturb to let the call through — then put all of it back when the call ends. It cannot promise a call will be audible in Silent mode, or through a stricter Do Not Disturb set by you or the device.
Calls are detected, but Do Not Disturb cannot be touched

The app can see who is calling and can raise the ring volume and switch out of Vibrate. It cannot ask Do Not Disturb to let the call through, because Do Not Disturb access has not been granted. While Do Not Disturb is on, a priority call will be silenced like any other.

Incoming calls reach the app with no caller number, so no caller can be identified and no priority call can ever be recognised. Nothing will ring differently, for anyone, until the essential permissions are granted.
This is not partial functionality. Nothing happens at all.

No priority contacts yet. Nothing will be treated as urgent until you add one.
Every priority contact is switched off, so no call will be treated as urgent.
This device reports a fixed output volume, so the ring volume cannot be changed by any app. Ringer mode can still be changed.
Add the people whose calls should get through. Everyone else is left completely alone — the app will not touch your sound settings for them.
%1$s will no longer be treated as a priority caller.

Matching compares the last digits of the number, so a call shown in a different format still matches.
Each permission below is listed with what the app cannot do without it. Nothing here is hidden behind a tick or a cross.
These grants can be changed at any time in system Settings. This screen re-checks them every time you open it, so what you see is what the system currently reports.
Permission not granted. The app has updated what it says it can do.
Android will no longer show that request. Opening app settings instead.
This device has no settings screen for that. Look for the app under Settings › Apps.
An essential permission is missing, so no call is being treated as urgent. The setup walkthrough asks for one permission at a time and explains what each one is for.
Without this, the app does nothing
Everything the app can be granted has been granted.
Every entry is deleted from this device. Anything that happens afterwards is logged as usual.
Priority calls, sound changes and anything that fails will appear here. Only the last 500 entries are kept.
No entries match the filter you picked.
How loud the ring stream is set when a priority contact calls. The previous volume is put back when the call ends.
The lowest setting is %1$d%%. A priority ringer that cannot be heard would be worse than none at all.
When the same priority contact calls again quickly, the ring goes to maximum and a full-screen alert is shown. Either rule below can trigger it.
Escalates after %1$d calls in %2$d minutes, or %3$d calls in %4$d minutes.
If the end of a call is never reported, your sound settings are put back after this long anyway. This is what stops the phone being left loud and off Do Not Disturb.
How to handle Do Not Disturb
What the app asks Do Not Disturb to do for the length of a priority call.
Leaves Do Not Disturb on and asks it to permit calls. The least invasive change to someone else\'s phone, and the default.
Turn Do Not Disturb off for the call
Switches Do Not Disturb off entirely until the call ends, then switches it back on. More likely to be audible, and a larger change to make on someone\'s behalf.
Silent mode is not the same as Vibrate, and an app cannot reliably make a phone on Silent audible. If the phone is on Silent, the app records that it stayed silent rather than pretending it worked.

Do Not Disturb belongs to you and the system. On Android 15 and later, a stricter Do Not Disturb wins over anything an app asks for. When that happens the app logs it and says so on the status screen.
Some manufacturers ignore ring volume and ringer changes made by other apps. The app checks the result of every change it makes and reports the ones that did not take effect.
Android tells the app about a call as the phone starts ringing, not before, so the first moment of the ringtone may be at the old volume.
Errors are recorded whatever this is set to. Turning logging off must not make failures invisible.

Simulating a call runs exactly the same code an incoming call does, on this device, with the permissions you have actually granted. Nothing is mocked and no permission result is faked — if something is missing, the simulation fails the same way a real call would.
A simulation really does change your ringer, volume and Do Not Disturb. They are put back by the same restore path a real call uses, and the button below forces it at any time.
Which contact should the simulated call come from?
This phone is not on Normal, so the simulation may play the backup alert out loud. There is no real call to end it — use Restore now, or wait for the auto-restore timer.
Simulating a repeat caller records the earlier calls it would take to reach your threshold (%1$d calls in %2$d minutes) and then places one more.
Add an enabled priority contact first.
Repeat-caller escalation is switched off in Settings.
Earlier calls recorded. Running the call now.
Simulation finished. Check the result below.
Puts the ringer mode, volume and Do Not Disturb back to whatever they were before the last priority call. Safe to press at any time.
A simulated call changed your settings. They will be restored automatically, or press the button.
Restore was incomplete. Check the activity log.
Every change the app attempted was blocked. A real call would not have sounded any different.
